title: Sticky rollout signal digest - 2027-11-29
content:
Attendees: Maya, Jordan, Priya, Samir, Esha (joined late), + Ops on call (Lars)

Purpose: quick weekly capture of signals and actions for the Panel/UI rollout that started last week. This doc is a sticky, informal runbook for signals we care about (latency deltas, error modes, UX regressions) and a short actions list to keep things moving.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Canary at 15% traffic on east-us for panel gating feature (flag: panel_v2).
- Small uptick in p95 token latency for short requests (<=64 tokens) in canary group: +22ms baseline but p99 unchanged.
- Two user-facing issues reported in support: slow initial render for heavy dashboards and one duplication of saved filters. Both reproducible, traced to client-side hydration timing and a dedupe edge-case in backend.
- Telemetry dashboards updated; primary follow-ups assigned.

Fresh signals / metrics snapshot (most recent 3 hours):
- Request volume (canary subset): 3.4k reqs
- Error rate (5xx) canary: 0.12% (baseline: 0.08%) — small bump attributable to a specific tensor-serve timeout path (see RT-2045)
- p50/p95/p99 token latencies (canary vs baseline):
  - p50: 14ms -> 16ms (+2ms)
  - p95: 82ms -> 104ms (+22ms)
  - p99: 360ms -> 362ms (+2ms)
- UI render time (first-contentful-paint median): 230ms -> 290ms for canary users on mobile
- Session drop (0.3% increase) for users hitting a specific opt-in flow (panel V2 beta)

What we checked already:
- Kernel selection/serving runtime: no abnormal evictions or GPU stalls during the window (SRE verified)
- Batch sizes: canary saw slightly higher small-sequence fractions — may explain token-level overhead
- Network: no region-wide infra incidents reported
- Feature flag rollout config: gradual linear ramp to 15% with 30m evaluation, auto-hold on >0.5% increase in 5xx (not tripped)

User reports (support + internal):
- SR-8712: "dashboard takes long to show charts" (user on iOS 17) — reproduction steps attached in ticket; snapshot shows client hydration waiting on /panels/init metadata call which had 120ms latency spike in canary traces.
- SR-8715: "saved filters duplicated when toggling panel" — traced to a client race on optimistic UI + server dedupe boundary; minor but high-visibility because it touches user data.

Open incidents / prioritization:
- Incident-ish: token-latency p95 increase (priority: P2). Action: instrument sampling at client and infra layers, add micro-traces in panel init path. Owner: Samir. ETA: small deploy with extra logs by 2027-11-30 09:00 PT.
- Bug: saved-filter duplication (priority: P1 for rollback gating if reproducible at scale). Feature flag safety: we can immediately mark panel_v2 as 'hold' for new accounts if duplication rate > 0.02% across sessions. Owner: Priya. ETA: hotfix PR in review (see linked PR).

Decisions made in meeting:
- Continue canary at 15% for another 24h but turn on stricter auto-hold threshold for dedupe bug (0.02% 5xx+deds). Rationale: latency deltas are small and p99 is stable, but duplication bug is UX-critical.
- Add an explicit client-side retry guard for saved-filter operations to avoid double-submit races while server-side fix lands. Quick patch accepted (Jordan).

Action items (owner / due):
- Samir: Roll an instrumented canary build that samples detailed token timings + panel init traces. Deploy by 2027-11-30 09:00 PT. Linked: RT-2045.
- Priya: Finalize and ship backend dedupe hotfix + add a migration-safe flag to make dedupe idempotent. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/891. Target merge -> canary re-eval 2027-11-30 14:00 PT.
- Jordan: Client quick patch to add debounce & single-flight guard for saved-filter writes; small release to canary by 2027-11-30 12:00 PT.
- Esha: Update telemetry dashboard tiles to show dedupe metric per region and per cohort (beta vs standard). ETA 2027-11-30 EOD.
- Maya: Coordinate CS communication draft for affected beta customers, include rollback plan and expected timelines. Draft by 2027-11-30 10:00 PT.
- Ops (Lars): Watcher during the 11/30 morning window, ready to trigger immediate hold if duplication >0.02% or 5xx >0.5%.

Blockers & questions:
- Need counts for how many active beta users are in canary cohort (product ask). Jordan to pull cohort size today.
- Telemetry sampling currently drops detailed token traces above 5k events/min; if we ramp sampling too much we hit quota. Ops/infra input needed to temporarily lift rate limit. Samir to sync with infra.
- Is the dedupe bug limited to saved-filters or across other optimistic writes? Priya to audit similar flows and report by EOD.

Parking lot (things to consider, not today):
- Evaluate client-side prefetching of panel metadata only for heavy dashboards to reduce hydration stalls (Priya / UX spike).
- Longer-term: surface per-model token-latency contribution in console (token-level cost/latency tradeoff) — Redwood Optimize tie-in.

Meeting notes, informal extras and scratch: 
- Jordan: "saw duplication locally only when toggling fast on dev build" => likely race.
- Samir: "batcher had more tiny sequences than expected; we can tune small-seq path".
- Maya: flagged customer empathy language for CS note: emphasize rollback option + timeline.

Next check-in: quick async update in #panel-rollouts channel around 2027-11-30 11:30 PT; synchronous follow-up if hotfix needs verification.

Links & artifacts: 
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/891
- Covering ticket: JIRA-RT-2045
- Eval dashboard (telemetry): https://internal-telemetry.redwood/panel-v2-canary
- Customer reports: SR-8712, SR-8715

Estimated follow-up timeline (rough):
- 2027-11-30 09:00 PT: instrumented canary deployment
- 2027-11-30 12:00 PT: client guard release
- 2027-11-30 14:00 PT: backend hotfix merge + canary monitoring window
- 2027-11-30 EOD: consolidate signals + decision to ramp/rollback

If anything spikes (duplication >0.02% or 5xx >0.5%), hold and notify execs + product (Maya to coordinate).

Raw notes / scratch (unpolished):
- should we flip to 10% and hold longer? pros: smaller signal noise; cons: slower validation for UX. Preference: keep 15% for now because we need broader client coverage.
- question: do we have end-to-end traces showing the fallback path for tensor timeouts? SRE: yes, see RT-2045 sampling.
- random thought: add a lightweight client-side telemetry flag specifically for beta cohorts to reduce noise in main dashboards.

-- end of sticky digest --
